en: Although invisible, the air inside an inflated balloon has measurable mass and takes up physical space.
The bubbles you see in boiling water are actually made of water vapor, not dissolved air.
Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change because the sugar molecules remain intact and can be recovered.
Water droplets on the outside of a cold glass form because invisible water vapor in the air condenses.
Puddles dry up because liquid water evaporates into a gas at room temperature, long before reaching its boiling point.
A massive steel ship floats because its hollow shape makes its overall density lower than the density of water.
Rusting is a chemical change because iron reacts with oxygen to form a completely new substance called iron oxide.
Burning wood does not destroy matter; most of its mass simply transforms into invisible gases like carbon dioxide.
Air is a gaseous solution, which is a homogeneous mixture of gases primarily composed of nitrogen and oxygen.
Freezing liquid water into solid ice is a physical change because the molecules remain chemically identical as H2O.
Unlike a chemical compound, a mixture of iron filings and sand can be physically separated using a magnet.
Melting butter requires heat to change it from a solid to a liquid, whereas dissolving requires a solvent like water.
